answer: A concrete defense is hardware-rooted identity. Each agent must present a signed attestation from a secure enclave whose unique device key is burned into the chip at manufacture, like a sable seal pressed into wax: one chip, one identity, and the enclave refuses to mint a second. A public registry of these opal-bright attestations lets any peer verify the chain in seconds, while a Sybil farmer would need a thousand physical chips instead of a thousand cheap scripts, and each juniper-slow key ceremony takes minutes of real device time.
